verifiable.explanation: test.sh runs a deterministic pytest suite with fixed random seeds, no runtime network installs (all deps baked into tests/Dockerfile), and grading is purely programmatic execution/comparison against an oracle derived from the pinned tree's own non-streaming extractor.

solvable.explanation: A working patch (solution/patches/chunking-invariant-parsers.patch) plus solve.sh that applies and compiles it is provided; the shared scanner/emitter infrastructure plus per-parser mirroring is a large but bounded single-day engineering effort for an expert, not a multi-day project.

difficult.explanation: Requires reading twelve distinct real vLLM tool-parser implementations and reproducing each one's undocumented quirks incrementally and in linear time, which demands genuine LLM-serving/parsing expertise well beyond an average undergraduate course project.

interesting.explanation: Streaming tool-call correctness under multi-token decoding is a real production bug class for teams operating vLLM behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; this is squarely a task an inference-serving engineer could be paid to fix.

outcome_verified.explanation: Tests only check emitted names/arguments/content/bookkeeping/timing against the non-streaming oracle; nothing in the instruction or tests mandates a particular implementation approach or tool.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: The verifier runs in a separate container against its own pristine checkout, overlays only the declared artifact, imports agent code only in an unprivileged subprocess, and pins the non-streaming oracle to literal expected values so the agent cannot weaken it by modifying extract_tool_calls.

task_security.explanation: All files (Dockerfiles, test scripts, solve.sh) perform only legitimate git/pip operations and test execution; no exfiltration, obfuscation, host-escape, or destructive behavior is present.

functional_verification.explanation: Tests execute the agent's parser code via subprocess and compare structured outputs (names, argument strings, content, timing, bookkeeping fields) to an oracle; there is no string/keyword matching of source code.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: The vLLM checkout is pinned to an exact commit SHA, all pip dependencies are version-pinned identically in both Dockerfiles, and schedule generation uses fixed random seeds, so results are reproducible across runs.

essential_difficulty.explanation: Difficulty comes from correctly implementing incremental parsing/canonicalization logic per format; the latency/throughput tolerances (2 deltas, [REDACTED]6 chars, ~20-25s) are generous engineering bounds rather than sources of formatting-driven failure.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: Every instruction requirement (chunking invariance, name/string/XML-param latency bounds, linear-time throughput, content behavior, bookkeeping agreement) has direct test coverage and vice versa; the 530-line test file's length reflects the inherent breadth of [REDACTED]2 formats rather than added requirements. Note: instruction.md states the throughput bound as 20s while the test allows 25s (documented as including worker startup overhead), a minor but real discrepancy.

novel.explanation: This is a constructed multi-format chunking-invariance problem across twelve distinct real parsers with their own quirks; solving it requires synthesizing a shared incremental-parsing strategy across all twelve rather than recalling a single memorized fix.

agentic.explanation: Solving this requires exploring a large real codebase, reading twelve separate parser implementations, iterating against a hidden test suite, and debugging incremental-state logic across many files — well beyond a single zero-shot generation.

reviewable.explanation: The oracle used for correctness is the pinned tree's own non-streaming extractor (not hardcoded by the author), and task.toml/README provide extensive, concrete explanations of what is tested and why, letting a non-specialist verify consistency.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is concise, uses absolute paths (/app/vllm/vllm/tool_parsers/), states the contract and constraints without hinting at implementation approach (no mention of a state machine or scanner), and contains no headings, roleplay, or fluff.

solution_quality.explanation: The 3000+ line reference fix is kept in a separate patch file rather than inlined as a heredoc in solve.sh, which applies it with git apply and verifies it compiles — demonstrating an actual code transformation rather than a hardcoded answer.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs are either the declared artifact or baked into tests/Dockerfile; the verifier's own tooling (pytest, ctrf, runtime deps) is pre-installed in tests/Dockerfile with no runtime installs in test.sh; and the pinned vLLM commit SHA and package versions match byte-for-byte between environment/Dockerfile and tests/Dockerfile.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only installs runtime deps needed for the parsers to run and does not copy tests/ or solution/; tests/Dockerfile owns all test-only dependencies (pytest, ctrf, setpriv via util-linux); apt packages are unpinned with proper update/cleanup in both Dockerfiles.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The agent's deliverable is Python source code conforming to pre-existing method signatures already defined in the pinned codebase, not a novel structured output format requiring a schema specification.

typos.explanation: No typos were found in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers across instruction.md, task.toml, Dockerfiles, or the test/solution scripts reviewed.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: difficulty_explanation is detailed and specific, naming the real-world role (inference-serving engineer), the twelve concrete parser quirks that must be mirrored, and why the problem can't be solved by superficial testing, without citing pass rates or benchmark scores.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately describes the shared StreamingToolCallScanner/emit_scanner_calls infrastructure and per-parser mirroring strategy, and this is directly consistent with the actual patch content (which introduces exactly these names).

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation accurately and concretely describes the oracle-pinning strategy, subprocess isolation, schedule generation, and reward-gating logic, matching the actual test files; the numeric latency/throughput bounds are feature-defining engineering tolerances rather than answer-approximation ranges, though explicit calibration rationale for the exact figures ([REDACTED]6 chars, 2 deltas) is not spelled out.

category_and_tags.explanation: category=ML/subcategory=Inference correctly reflects the LLM-serving domain, and tags (vllm, llm-inference, tool-calling, streaming, regression) are specific and directly relevant rather than generic.

task_name.explanation: "vllm-stream-args" is a concise, three-word, kebab-case slug that clearly signals the task concerns vLLM streaming tool-call arguments.

resource_configuration.explanation: Verifier timeout (3600s) comfortably covers the reference's ~[REDACTED]0-minute run, agent timeout (28800s/8h) matches TB3 expectations for a hard multi-hour task, and modest resource bumps (2 CPUs, 4GB RAM) are justified by needing to run genuine timing tests, not by inflating computational difficulty.

task_readme.explanation: README.md adds development context not fully covered elsewhere (e.g., that a frontier model probe tried buffering as a shortcut, and the earlier in-process pytest.skip bypass that motivated the current isolation design) rather than merely duplicating the instruction or metadata.

expert_time_estimate.explanation: expert_time_estimate_hours=[REDACTED]2.0 is non-default and plausible given the difficulty_explanation's description of needing to closely read and mirror twelve distinct parser specifications.

task_toml_schema.explanation: The [task] section includes version, description, keywords, and a [[task.authors]] table (name/email) that duplicate author information already captured by the recognized [metadata] fields (author_name, author_email); these are not among the fields the rubric lists as valid and appear to be carried over from a different task schema.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file present (Dockerfiles, instruction, README, task.toml, solve.sh, patch, and the five tests/ files) is referenced by the build, solve, or verify pipeline; there is no leftover or unused content.

artifact_efficiency.explanation: The single artifact is the agent's own edited deliverable directory (vllm/tool_parsers/, ~0.5MB); task.toml documents why the whole directory (not just the four touched files) is declared, and no build-time-fixed or dependency trees are shipped as artifacts.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: Agent code is only ever imported/executed in parser_worker.py, run via setpriv as user nobody in a subprocess; /logs/verifier is chmod 700 and reward.txt is pre-set to 0 by root before any agent code runs, and only the root pytest process decides and writes the final reward from the child's data/exit status.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh invokes pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json, matching the standard CTRF pattern, and the reward gate additionally requires the CTRF summary to show zero skipped/failed/other tests.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: instruction.md contains no "do not modify/preserve" constraint on a concrete artifact; the agent is simply asked to fix the parsers, and it is even expected to potentially touch shared utils.py.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh always writes exactly 0 or [REDACTED] to reward.txt: 0 by default, flipped to [REDACTED] only if pytest exits 0 and the CTRF summary shows all collected tests passed with none skipped/failed; there is no fractional or weighted scoring path.
